text:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 (p99 > 2.5s) · severity: P1 · paging oncall

maya: seeing the same on Wavefront dashboard — tail latency jump at ~14:07 UTC, cluster red.

alex: assigning @maya as primary oncall. Maya, do you want the bridge?

maya: yes please, starting quick bridge. tagging @charlie for infra visibility.

charlie: I can look at node-level metrics — might be a KV cache thrash or heap GC. shifting some traffic off eu-west-1 to eu-central as temp mitigation.

priya: CS asking if any customers impacted yet. @cs-lead any reports?

cs-lead: not yet from support but a couple of latency complaints coming in from EU-early-adopters. I'm prepping a short customer note if we need it.

maya: quick checks: 1) confirm rolling GC? 2) queue depth on frontend 3) kvcache hit-rate drop?

alex: running recommended queries now:
```
# Wavefront/PromQL-ish queries pasted for quick triage
max_over_time(latency_p99{route="/v1/generate", region="eu-west-1"}[5m])
rate(kv_cache_miss_total{region="eu-west-1"}[1m])
sum(rate(request_queue_length{pod=~"gen.*"}[1m])) by (pod)
```

alex: p99 spikes correlate with sharp rise in kv_cache_miss and one gen pod (gen-7) showing very high req queue length.

charlie: I see gen-7 had repeated OOMs and restarted 3x around 14:05. suspect degraded instance causing backpressure.

ben: oncall-ops suggestion: cordon gen-7 and drain, then bounce pool. Also switch routing policy to prefer eu-central for new requests while we heal.

maya: doing a quick cordon now: `kubectl cordon gen-7 && kubectl drain gen-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

maya: drained and restarted podset. Watching for p99 to fall.

priya: can we enable model-variant fallback for eu-west-1 to a smaller-quantized model to reduce token latency if we see another degradation?

alex: yes, putting a temporary rollout policy to favor quantized-8bit-variant for the route for 10min. Command applied.

incident-bot: Deploy note: rollout policy applied by alex at 14:15 UTC.

maya: p99 dropped from ~2.7s to ~0.9s across the cluster after drain + routing shift + variant fallback. Tail latency still has small spikes ~600ms, but under SLO for now.

charlie: root cause hypothesis: a combination of pod memory leak (OOMs) leading to queueing + cascading KV cache evictions increasing cold-KV lookups.

ben: opened issue infra#2345 to track gen-7 memory regression and kvcache eviction tuning. tagging eng-runtime.

priya: CS-lead, recommend holding off customer comms until we confirm stabilization and RCA. If complaints increase, send holding message referencing we are investigating a latency spike in EU and routing failovers applied.

cs-lead: got it. I'll prepare a short message ready to send if we see >5 customer incidents in next 30m.

maya: going to keep watch for 20m, will escalate if p99 creeps back. Adding short postmortem checklist to the thread: collect heapdumps from gen-7, kvcache eviction logs, service traces for affected time window, and snapshot traffic shift logs.

alex: pulling traces and flamegraphs now and saving to /tmp/incidents/3750002468/ — will attach to the ticket.

incident-bot: PAGING RESOLVE: automated alert cleared at 14:25 UTC (p99 back within threshold). Please continue monitoring.

maya: marking handoff to oncall-rotation for 14:30–15:00. If anything reappears, page oncall again.

charlie: quick follow-up: I'll respin pool with updated GC flags and increase kvcache size by 10% in the canary.

ben: noted. tracking mitigation actions in infra#2345 and ops-runbook update required for kvcache eviction threshold.

maya: thanks team. short RCA and full postmortem draft will be posted in #postmortems after collecting artifacts.

priya: thanks — keeping CS on standby.

cs-lead: sending a follow-up note to affected beta customers: "We've applied routing and model fallbacks to mitigate an EU latency spike; engineering is investigating root cause. We'll update within 4 hours."

maya: thread closed for active mitigation, leaving thread open for RCA attachments.
